## Update (2026-11-02): slimmed to nine optimizations, one per commit

This revision is rebased onto `main` `57bfde9f2c` and keeps nine optimizations, one per commit. Four earlier changes whose isolated throughput effects were within run-to-run noise were removed (see "Removed"). The previous seven-commit description is kept below for reference.

### Per-commit changes and measured effect

Measured on Qwen3.5 (GB300) with the NVIDIA plugin enabled. "Disable" = throughput change when only this commit is turned off in the full stack (one 1200 s AgentX trace-replay run per arm, TPS/user P50 / P90; run-to-run noise ≈2% at TP8 c16 and ≈1.4% at TEP8). "Static" = cumulative per-batch decode TPS/user change when the commit is added on top of the previous ones (identical requests, warmed rounds). Effects are not additive across commits.

| # | Commit | Change | Production / tests | Measured effect |
|---|---|---|---:|---|
| 1 | `d0385b181d` | Verify on vocabulary shards (no full-vocabulary logits gather) | +1299/−47 · +331/−8 | Disable: TP8 PD c16 −3.6% / −1.8%; TEP8 PD c272 −8.1% / −5.9%. Static gain appears together with #2 (switch is wired there) |
| 2 | `8bbfc2c3ab` | Capture the post-verify tail (sampling, acceptance, output prep in one graph) | +671/−116 · +168/−54 | Static (with #1): TP8 B1/8/16/32/64 +4.2/+2.1/+4.8/+6.3/+10.0%; TEP8 B8/16/32/64/128 +3.7/+6.1/+7.0/+11.0/+14.1% |
| 3 | `b19e38a511` | Keep unchanged top-1 / hidden-state relay rows in private graph buffers (includes alias fix) | +208/−34 · +127/−4 | Disable: TP8 PD c16 −4.0% / −3.7%; TEP8 c272 −1.1% / −0.4% (within noise) |
| 4 | `15aa4dfede` | Share draft attention metadata and fused-path policies | +201/−19 · +363/−9 | Disable: TEP8 PD c272 −6.6% / −4.2%; TP8 c16 −0.6% / −1.6% (within noise). Static TEP8 B8–B128 +7.5% to +12.5% |
| 5 | `018b707117` | Defer staging KV scatters to between decode forwards | +327/−71 · +69/−1 | Add: TEP8 PD c130 +4.1% / +3.4% |
| 6 | `b50357ff68` | Read staging metadata asynchronously (pinned, fenced) | +44/−13 · +79/−0 | Add: TEP8 PD c130 +3.8% / +9.1%; TEP8 PD c272 +11.9% / +19.2% |
| 7 | `35039280b3` | Overlap PD decode admission with the in-flight forward | +63/−10 · +114/−0 | Leave-one-out gain at DEP8 PD c704: +4.5% / +20.3% (TP8 / TEP8 points not measured separately) |
| 8 | `ef001f9d5f` | Reuse attention length-group plans within a forward | +140/−0 · +167/−0 | Leave-one-out gain at DEP8 PD c704: +5.2% / +14.5% |
| 9 | `49c9a41235` | Record draft-extend read completion in the graph and guard KV-page reuse | +102/−7 · +82/−2 | Leave-one-out gain at DEP8 PD c704: +4.3% / +15.0% |
| 10 | `0e7516f9b4` | Reserve decode staging only for the chunks covered by the current prefill batch, instead of a long request's whole length at its first chunk (the staging FIFO no longer waits on chunks that have not been computed) | +17/−3 · +53/−0 | Add, TEP8 PD concurrency 272 (same-time control, one 1200 s run each): **TTFT P90 −53.3% (1.87 → 0.88 s)**, E2E latency P90 −4.4%, TPS/user P50 +0.4% / P90 −1.1%. Prefill KV-transfer stage mean 380 → 159 ms. Follows the runtime master switch; with it off, or for dummy / unsupported managers, the whole-request reservation is kept. CPU per commit: no new failures; TEP8 GSM8K 10/10 |

Total (ten commits): production +3067 / −288, tests +1712 / −73 (the previous revision was production +5148 / −358, tests +4386).

### Removed

| Removed change | Production lines | Measured effect when disabled alone |
|---|---:|---|
| Single-launch ReplaySSM state commit | +953 | TP8 c16 −0.0% / −1.2%; TEP8 c272 −0.6% / −1.1% |
| Decode scratch / host-copy pooling | +347 | TP8 c16 −1.2% / −1.3%; not active under EP |
| Per-shape fill / copy-plan reuse | +412 | TP8 c16 −0.2% / +1.6%; not active under EP |
| Preparing the next draft round early | +1409 | TP8 c16 −0.4% / −2.8%; not active under EP |

Each is within run-to-run noise on its own. Disabling all four together, measured three times per arm at TP8 PD concurrency 16 (one prefill + two TP8 decode workers, 1200 s each, all valid):

| Arm | TPS/user P50 (min–max) | TPS/user P90 (min–max) |
|---|---:|---:|
| All four enabled | 1380.3 (1377.3–1384.2) | 894.5 (859.6–913.6) |
| All four disabled | 1335.0 (1332.8–1338.1) | 902.9 (883.9–925.5) |
| Difference of means | −3.3% | +0.9% |

The P50 ranges do not overlap, so removing the four together costs about 3% at P50 at this point; P90 is within its spread. The two groups ran about 1.5 h apart. Fused EAGLE index preparation is left for a follow-up.

### Default behavior (runtime master switch off)

`SGLANG_ENABLE_NV_MEGA_RUNTIME_OPTIMIZATION` defaults to off, and its child switches follow it. With it off, execution matches `main`:
- EAGLE / multi-layer / UNO / NGRAM eager verify calls `eagle_sample` with the same arguments as `main` (no provider hooks or post-verify views are built).
- The asynchronous staging-metadata readback is not used; the original synchronous path runs.
- FlashMLA stays in the draft-extend graph-supported backend list, as on `main`.

Remaining differences on the default path are structural only and do not change execution: new dataclass fields with defaults, attribute initialization, imports, the decode admission `wait_stream` placement (same position relative to `prepare_for_prebuilt` and the KV checksum, with no GPU work between), and one `.to(bonus.dtype)` cast in the existing verify-commit Triton kernel that is a no-op for the default `int32` bonus buffer. Paths that remove clones, take the FP8 pre-quantized input, add the staging chunk-arrival lock, or pass an LM-head `out=` buffer are reached only through the optimized (switch-on or plugin) callers.

Validation of this head: per-commit CPU tests on `main` plus all ten prefixes (no new failures); GSM8K 10/10 with the switch off and the plugin off (TP8). GSM8K 10/10 with the switch on (TEP8, with #47201 and the plugin).

### Integration order

Merge #47201 first, then this PR, then enable the plugin. This PR keeps optional contract discovery and stock fallbacks; the plugin uses the provider contracts from #47201.

### Validation

- CPU: `main` and each of the nine commit prefixes run the same relevant unit tests; 0 failed relative to `main` (`main` has two pre-existing failures, unchanged).
- GSM8K (10 questions, real acceptance) with #47201 and the plugin: TP8 10/10 and TEP8 (EP4) 10/10, strict and flexible, no empty responses.
- End-to-end AgentX for this exact revision (with #47201 and the plugin; one 1200 s run per point, all valid, zero errored requests). "Full stack" is the same deployment with the four removed commits still included:

| Point | This revision TPS/user P50 / P90 | vs full stack |
|---|---:|---:|
| TP8 PD, concurrency 16 | 1051.6 / 792.3 | −1.2% / −0.8% |
| TP8 PD, concurrency 128 | 665.3 / 544.3 | +0.2% / −2.7% |
| TEP8 PD, concurrency 130 | 484.5 / 348.0 | −0.5% / −3.0% |
| TEP8 PD, concurrency 272 | 301.2 / 206.1 | −2.3% / −3.6% |

  P50 is within run-to-run noise (≈2% TP8, ≈1.4% TEP8) at three of four points; P90 is 2.7–3.6% lower at three points (single runs). Against `main` (`efdcb420c7` with the released plugin installed unmodified, megakernel off), TEP8 PD at concurrency 272, same recipe and window, one 1200 s run each:

  | Metric | `main` | `main` + #47201 + this PR + plugin | change |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|
  | TPS/user P50 / P90 | 87.5 / 83.1 | 301.2 / 206.1 | +244% / +148% |
  | TTFT P90 (s) | 8.02 | 1.99 | −75% |
  | E2E latency P90 (s) | 24.25 | 8.37 | −65% |
  | Total tok/s/GPU | 64569 | 89732 | +39% |

  This is the full stack (binding, runtime and plugin together) and is not attributed to this PR alone.

<details>
<summary>Previous revision description (seven commits)</summary>

## Motivation

Speculative decoding performs many small index-building launches, copies, allocations, graph metadata updates, and recurrent-state operations between draft rounds. This PR adds model-independent, capability-checked fast paths while retaining the existing SGLang implementation as the fallback.

This PR contains runtime optimizations only: no provider ABI, provider factory, model-name check, or Qwen-specific kernel policy. It is based directly on `main` and does not depend on the companion binding PR.

**Switch inventory:** this standalone runtime tree has **28** Boolean child switches that follow `SGLANG_ENABLE_NV_MEGA_RUNTIME_OPTIMIZATION` when unset. The base `main` supplies 27; R7 adds exactly one, `SGLANG_TRTL3_EP_DEFER_FINALIZE`, as the 28th. This PR declares no other master-following child switch.

| ID | Purpose | Switch |
|---|---|---|
| R1 | Verify directly on vocabulary shards | `SGLANG_ENABLE_NV_MEGA_RUNTIME_OPTIMIZATION` |
| R2 | Fuse EAGLE index preparation | Master switch |
| R3 | Prepare the next EAGLE draft round | `SGLANG_ENABLE_EAGLE_POST_VERIFY_CUDA_GRAPH` inherits master when unset |
| R4 | Capture the EAGLE post-verify tail | Master + post-verify graph switch |
| R5 | Commit ReplaySSM state in one CUDA launch | Master switch |
| R6 | Capture generic GDN prefill state updates | `SGLANG_ENABLE_GDN_PREFILL_GRAPH_EXTEND` inherits master when unset |
| R7 | Reuse graph resources and speculative relays | Master; explicit child values take precedence |

## Modifications

### R1 — Verify directly on vocabulary shards

- **What:** Produce native or provider-supplied token keys from rank-local vocabulary logits and reduce the compact keys across tensor-parallel ranks. SGLang owns the reducer and every collective.
- **Why:** Greedy verification needs only the winning token, so this avoids a full-logit all-gather, temporary full-vocabulary tensor, and following argmax.
- **Switch:** `SGLANG_ENABLE_NV_MEGA_RUNTIME_OPTIMIZATION`.
- **Fallback:** Sampling, penalties, watermarking, logprob requests, provider decline, or a consumer without shard support returns to the original full-logit gather and verifier before provider RNG is consumed.

### R2 — Fuse EAGLE index preparation

- **What:** Fuse chain-tree construction, draft-extend layout, draft/cache locations, positions, and mRoPE indices in generic CUDA kernels.
- **Why:** Remove repeated small launches and intermediate tensors from model-neutral EAGLE index production.
- **Switch:** The master runtime switch.
- **Fallback:** Dtype, layout, shape, or device rejection occurs before JIT loading and uses the existing Triton/stock producers.

### R3 — Prepare the next EAGLE draft round

- **What:** During post-verify, stage request rows, accepted sequence lengths, positions, and KV write-window locations directly into the next draft graph's static buffers. A fresh host key and one-shot lease guard request-pool reuse; scheduler and runner tensors remain distinct.
- **Why:** Avoid returning through a scheduler gather and runner copy when the next graph-compatible destination is already known.
- **Switch:** `SGLANG_ENABLE_EAGLE_POST_VERIFY_CUDA_GRAPH`; when unset it follows the master switch, while an explicit value takes precedence.
- **Fallback:** Unsupported algorithm, top-k, EP/layout, graph miss, stale key, invalid lease, or insufficient reservation executes the original scheduler gather and runner copy.

### R4 — Capture the EAGLE post-verify tail

- **What:** Fuse chain acceptance and, for compatible cases, capture sampling, acceptance, commit-output preparation, and next-draft layout. Eager, graph, EAGLE, MultiLayerEAGLE, NGRAM, and UNO paths call one always-present strategy; runtime-only builds resolve a structural stock strategy.
- **Why:** Remove the multi-launch eager tail while keeping the stock verifier authoritative outside the graph contract.
- **Switch:** Fused chain acceptance uses the master switch. Capture/replay uses `SGLANG_ENABLE_EAGLE_POST_VERIFY_CUDA_GRAPH`, which follows the master only when unset.
- **Fallback:** Missing binding capability, unsupported device/tree/sampling/watermark/graph key, or provider decline invokes `eagle_sample` and the original eager path.

### R5 — Commit ReplaySSM state in one CUDA launch

- **What:** Fold accepted rows and update circular cache, tracking rows, cursor, and stable state in one generic CUDA launch before unchanged circular-fold bookkeeping.
- **Why:** Replace a multi-operation Triton state update and its intermediate launches/traffic.
- **Switch:** The master runtime switch only.
- **Fallback:** BF16, contiguous layout, supported shape/index, SM90+, CUDA binding availability, and successful NVRTC prebuild are all required; any miss uses the stock Triton commit. The CUDA path changes FP32 accumulation order and is tolerance-equivalent at `rtol=2^-7, atol=1e-6`, not bitwise-equivalent.

### R6 — Capture generic GDN prefill state updates

- **What:** Capture compatible GDN prefill/extend state tracking and FlashInfer calls in reusable CUDA graphs with caller-owned dynamic-input bridges.
- **Why:** Remove repeated host dispatch and allocation at graph-stable shapes.
- **Switch:** `SGLANG_ENABLE_GDN_PREFILL_GRAPH_EXTEND`; when unset it follows the master, while an explicit value takes precedence.
- **Fallback:** Unsupported mode, shape, graph size, backend, or capture error uses the existing eager implementation.

### R7 — Reuse graph resources and speculative relays

- **What:** Pool speculative tensors/events, reuse graph buffers and TRT graph metadata, batch small field copies, retain unchanged top-k-1 relay rows, and skip allocation work when prepared-next already owns the destination. It also adds capability-checked FP8 prequantized-input reuse, MNNVL shape/EP tuning, EP deferred finalization, and an optional lazy FlashMLA graph import.
- **Why:** Remove repeated allocation, copy, metadata construction, synchronization, and backend setup at draft/verify boundaries.
- **Switch:** The master runtime switch. R7 declares `SGLANG_TRTL3_EP_DEFER_FINALIZE` as the 28th master-following child; it and the 27 inherited child controls honor explicit `0` or `1` values before inheriting the master.
- **Fallback:** Shape, EP, backend, layout, graph-lifetime, or optional-import rejection performs the original copy, allocation, metadata construction, finalize, or backend path.

### Independence and composition with #47201

This PR and #47201 are independently based on `main`; neither is a merge prerequisite for the other. When the second PR is rebased after the first lands, or when both are composed before merge, their EAGLE changes overlap in exactly five files:

- `eagle_draft_cuda_graph_runner.py`
- `eagle_draft_extend_cuda_graph_runner.py`
- `eagle_megakernel.py`
- `eagle_worker_v2.py`
- `test_eagle_binding.py`

The later PR should retain this PR's relay/static-buffer behavior and #47201's always-present facade while resolving those overlaps. The combined focused suite covers that composition.

The composed branches have five ordering adapters (`speculative_runtime.py`, `eagle_post_verify_graphs.py`, `eagle_utils.py`, `eagle_worker_common.py`, and `sharded_verify.py`) and six test ownership/fixture changes (`test_speculative_runtime_contract.py`, `test_speculative_runtime_hooks.py`, `test_speculative_runtime_hook_execution.py`, `test_sharded_verify.py`, `test_megakernel_guards.py`, and `test_dspark_step_inputs_once.py`). The adapters cache optional capability lookup and provide standalone stock fallbacks. With both PRs present they resolve to the same canonical views, provider callback, reducer, collectives, and optimized dispatch; they change no kernel, graph launch, shape eligibility, plugin selector, or autotune snapshot.

## Accuracy Tests

- Every R1–R7 commit independently completes changed-file `compileall`; the complete runtime tree also completes import smoke and full relevant-directory compilation.
- Runtime-only focused CPU result: **276 passed, 21 skipped, 2,684 subtests passed**.
- Combined runtime-plus-binding focused CPU result: **302 passed, 18 skipped, 2,726 subtests passed**.
- Master-off tests cover stock identity and bypass for sharded verification, prepared-next, ReplaySSM commit, GDN prefill graphs, resource reuse, and explicit child-switch overrides. Unsupported consumers preserve the full-vocabulary stock path.
- A no-simulation serving run completed GSM10 with **10/10** answers. An integrated serving run also completed a 53-request long-context replay.
- Layer-by-layer localization found no numerical difference before the ReplaySSM committed state. At that first difference, 233 of 5,898,240 BF16 elements differed, all within `atol=1e-6, rtol=2^-7`; this state is tolerance-equivalent, not bitwise-equivalent.
- In a real two-request TEP8 verify batch, all eight ranks compared 434,560 provider-slot logits and 57,344 hidden-state values with the stock computation and found zero bitwise differences.
- DEP8 with only the master switch enabled (runtime only, without Qwen3.5 plugin enablement) completed no-simulation greedy GSM10 with **10/10** answers.
- Greedy default verification, including requests carrying seeds, is bitwise identical to direct stock behavior.

GSM8K on the current head, no draft-acceptance simulation, seed 1234 (strict / flexible accuracy):

| Topology | 1319 questions, greedy | 250 questions, greedy | 250 questions, sampled T=1.0 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TP8 | `0.978 / 0.977` | `0.988 / 0.988` | `0.972 / 0.972` |
| TEP8 | `0.980 / 0.979` | `0.980 / 0.980` | `0.968 / 0.968` |

No empty responses in any run. TP8 also passed a 53-request long-context replay (three attempts, all 53/53, no CUDA errors).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Static decode uses identical requests and warmed, unprofiled rounds; P50/P90 TPS/user is derived from round latency. Autotune selections were frozen for all measurements in both columns; TP8 B1 was measured before the latest plugin commit, which does not affect the single-request path; all other rows were measured on the current head.

| Topology | Batch | main P50/P90 TPS/user | this PR P50/P90 TPS/user | change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| TP8 | 1 | `773.39 / 753.59` | `1561.443 / 1553.168` | `+101.9% / +106.1%` |
| TP8 | 8 | `492.46 / 488.33` | `657.33 / 650.93` | `+33.5% / +33.3%` |
| TP8 | 16 | `410.25 / 406.68` | `553.19 / 546.35` | `+34.8% / +34.3%` |
| TP8 | 64 | `260.23 / 258.97` | `324.28 / 323.57` | `+24.6% / +24.9%` |
| TEP8 | 32 | `359.99 / 357.98` | `431.472 / 428.328` | `+19.9% / +19.7%` |
| TEP8 | 64 | `283.69 / 282.05` | `351.007 / 348.592` | `+23.7% / +23.6%` |
| TEP8 | 128 | `201.43 / 200.51` | `258.757 / 257.732` | `+28.5% / +28.5%` |

Here, `main` means upstream SGLang with the master switch disabled and no optional megakernel plugin installed. 

AgentX trace replay, 3600 s window, TEP8 prefill/decode disaggregation at concurrency 272, same request set and the same fixed draft acceptance length in both columns:

| Metric | main | this PR | change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TPS/user P50 / P90 | `85.48 / 81.31` | `129.37 / 112.92` | `+51.3% / +38.9%` |

TP8 decode with prefill/decode disaggregation at concurrency 128 (1 prefill + 4 decode nodes), same settings:

|---|---:|---:|---:|

All columns of all AgentX tables completed the full window with zero errored requests.

## Known limitations

- TP8 B8/B16 are path-equivalent measurements from an earlier revision rather than direct measurements of the current composition.
- A per-segment `main` comparison for total, verify, and draft time is not yet available.
- The full three-part serving accuracy suite has not been rerun on the current composition.
- Rebasing one SGLang PR after the other lands, or stacking them before merge, requires the documented five-file resolution.

## Checklist

- [x] Format changed code according to the SGLang contribution guide.
- [x] Add focused unit tests for every runtime fast path and stock fallback.
- [x] Update runtime environment-variable documentation and fallback contracts.
- [x] Keep model-specific kernels and policy out of this runtime PR.
- [x] Add matching `main` static measurements, serving accuracy (GSM8K), and AgentX results.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code-style guidance.

</details>

### Default behavior (runtime master switch off)

`SGLANG_ENABLE_NV_MEGA_RUNTIME_OPTIMIZATION` defaults to off, and its child switches follow it. With it off, execution matches `main`:
- EAGLE / multi-layer / UNO / NGRAM eager verify calls `eagle_sample` with the same arguments as `main` (no provider hooks or post-verify views are built).
- The asynchronous staging-metadata readback is not used; the original synchronous path runs.
- FlashMLA stays in the draft-extend graph-supported backend list, as on `main`.

Remaining differences on the default path are structural only and do not change execution: new dataclass fields with defaults, attribute initialization, imports, the decode admission `wait_stream` placement (same position relative to `prepare_for_prebuilt` and the KV checksum, with no GPU work between), and one `.to(bonus.dtype)` cast in the existing verify-commit Triton kernel that is a no-op for the default `int32` bonus buffer. Paths that remove clones, take the FP8 pre-quantized input, add the staging chunk-arrival lock, or pass an LM-head `out=` buffer are reached only through the optimized (switch-on or plugin) callers.

## Motivation

Speculative decoding performs many small index-building launches, copies, allocations, graph metadata updates, and recurrent-state operations between draft rounds. This PR adds model-independent, capability-checked fast paths while retaining the existing SGLang implementation as the fallback.

This PR contains runtime optimizations only: no provider ABI, provider factory, model-name check, or Qwen-specific kernel policy. It is based directly on `main` and does not depend on the companion binding PR.

**Switch inventory:** this standalone runtime tree has **28** Boolean child switches that follow `SGLANG_ENABLE_NV_MEGA_RUNTIME_OPTIMIZATION` when unset. The base `main` supplies 27; R7 adds exactly one, `SGLANG_TRTL3_EP_DEFER_FINALIZE`, as the 28th. This PR declares no other master-following child switch.

| ID | Purpose | Switch |
|---|---|---|
| R1 | Verify directly on vocabulary shards | `SGLANG_ENABLE_NV_MEGA_RUNTIME_OPTIMIZATION` |
| R2 | Fuse EAGLE index preparation | Master switch |
| R3 | Prepare the next EAGLE draft round | `SGLANG_ENABLE_EAGLE_POST_VERIFY_CUDA_GRAPH` inherits master when unset |
| R4 | Capture the EAGLE post-verify tail | Master + post-verify graph switch |
| R5 | Commit ReplaySSM state in one CUDA launch | Master switch |
| R6 | Capture generic GDN prefill state updates | `SGLANG_ENABLE_GDN_PREFILL_GRAPH_EXTEND` inherits master when unset |
| R7 | Reuse graph resources and speculative relays | Master; explicit child values take precedence |

## Modifications

### R1 — Verify directly on vocabulary shards

- **What:** Produce native or provider-supplied token keys from rank-local vocabulary logits and reduce the compact keys across tensor-parallel ranks. SGLang owns the reducer and every collective.
- **Why:** Greedy verification needs only the winning token, so this avoids a full-logit all-gather, temporary full-vocabulary tensor, and following argmax.
- **Switch:** `SGLANG_ENABLE_NV_MEGA_RUNTIME_OPTIMIZATION`.
- **Fallback:** Sampling, penalties, watermarking, logprob requests, provider decline, or a consumer without shard support returns to the original full-logit gather and verifier before provider RNG is consumed.

### R2 — Fuse EAGLE index preparation

- **What:** Fuse chain-tree construction, draft-extend layout, draft/cache locations, positions, and mRoPE indices in generic CUDA kernels.
- **Why:** Remove repeated small launches and intermediate tensors from model-neutral EAGLE index production.
- **Switch:** The master runtime switch.
- **Fallback:** Dtype, layout, shape, or device rejection occurs before JIT loading and uses the existing Triton/stock producers.

### R3 — Prepare the next EAGLE draft round

- **What:** During post-verify, stage request rows, accepted sequence lengths, positions, and KV write-window locations directly into the next draft graph's static buffers. A fresh host key and one-shot lease guard request-pool reuse; scheduler and runner tensors remain distinct.
- **Why:** Avoid returning through a scheduler gather and runner copy when the next graph-compatible destination is already known.
- **Switch:** `SGLANG_ENABLE_EAGLE_POST_VERIFY_CUDA_GRAPH`; when unset it follows the master switch, while an explicit value takes precedence.
- **Fallback:** Unsupported algorithm, top-k, EP/layout, graph miss, stale key, invalid lease, or insufficient reservation executes the original scheduler gather and runner copy.

### R4 — Capture the EAGLE post-verify tail

- **What:** Fuse chain acceptance and, for compatible cases, capture sampling, acceptance, commit-output preparation, and next-draft layout. Eager, graph, EAGLE, MultiLayerEAGLE, NGRAM, and UNO paths call one always-present strategy; runtime-only builds resolve a structural stock strategy.
- **Why:** Remove the multi-launch eager tail while keeping the stock verifier authoritative outside the graph contract.
- **Switch:** Fused chain acceptance uses the master switch. Capture/replay uses `SGLANG_ENABLE_EAGLE_POST_VERIFY_CUDA_GRAPH`, which follows the master only when unset.
- **Fallback:** Missing binding capability, unsupported device/tree/sampling/watermark/graph key, or provider decline invokes `eagle_sample` and the original eager path.

### R5 — Commit ReplaySSM state in one CUDA launch

- **What:** Fold accepted rows and update circular cache, tracking rows, cursor, and stable state in one generic CUDA launch before unchanged circular-fold bookkeeping.
- **Why:** Replace a multi-operation Triton state update and its intermediate launches/traffic.
- **Switch:** The master runtime switch only.
- **Fallback:** BF16, contiguous layout, supported shape/index, SM90+, CUDA binding availability, and successful NVRTC prebuild are all required; any miss uses the stock Triton commit. The CUDA path changes FP32 accumulation order and is tolerance-equivalent at `rtol=2^-7, atol=1e-6`, not bitwise-equivalent.

### R6 — Capture generic GDN prefill state updates

- **What:** Capture compatible GDN prefill/extend state tracking and FlashInfer calls in reusable CUDA graphs with caller-owned dynamic-input bridges.
- **Why:** Remove repeated host dispatch and allocation at graph-stable shapes.
- **Switch:** `SGLANG_ENABLE_GDN_PREFILL_GRAPH_EXTEND`; when unset it follows the master, while an explicit value takes precedence.
- **Fallback:** Unsupported mode, shape, graph size, backend, or capture error uses the existing eager implementation.

### R7 — Reuse graph resources and speculative relays

- **What:** Pool speculative tensors/events, reuse graph buffers and TRT graph metadata, batch small field copies, retain unchanged top-k-1 relay rows, and skip allocation work when prepared-next already owns the destination. It also adds capability-checked FP8 prequantized-input reuse, MNNVL shape/EP tuning, EP deferred finalization, and an optional lazy FlashMLA graph import.
- **Why:** Remove repeated allocation, copy, metadata construction, synchronization, and backend setup at draft/verify boundaries.
- **Switch:** The master runtime switch. R7 declares `SGLANG_TRTL3_EP_DEFER_FINALIZE` as the 28th master-following child; it and the 27 inherited child controls honor explicit `0` or `1` values before inheriting the master.
- **Fallback:** Shape, EP, backend, layout, graph-lifetime, or optional-import rejection performs the original copy, allocation, metadata construction, finalize, or backend path.

### Independence and composition with #47201

This PR and #47201 are independently based on `main`; neither is a merge prerequisite for the other. When the second PR is rebased after the first lands, or when both are composed before merge, their EAGLE changes overlap in exactly five files:

- `eagle_draft_cuda_graph_runner.py`
- `eagle_draft_extend_cuda_graph_runner.py`
- `eagle_megakernel.py`
- `eagle_worker_v2.py`
- `test_eagle_binding.py`

The later PR should retain this PR's relay/static-buffer behavior and #47201's always-present facade while resolving those overlaps. The combined focused suite covers that composition.

The composed branches have five ordering adapters (`speculative_runtime.py`, `eagle_post_verify_graphs.py`, `eagle_utils.py`, `eagle_worker_common.py`, and `sharded_verify.py`) and six test ownership/fixture changes (`test_speculative_runtime_contract.py`, `test_speculative_runtime_hooks.py`, `test_speculative_runtime_hook_execution.py`, `test_sharded_verify.py`, `test_megakernel_guards.py`, and `test_dspark_step_inputs_once.py`). The adapters cache optional capability lookup and provide standalone stock fallbacks. With both PRs present they resolve to the same canonical views, provider callback, reducer, collectives, and optimized dispatch; they change no kernel, graph launch, shape eligibility, plugin selector, or autotune snapshot.

## Accuracy Tests

- Every R1–R7 commit independently completes changed-file `compileall`; the complete runtime tree also completes import smoke and full relevant-directory compilation.
- Runtime-only focused CPU result: **276 passed, 21 skipped, 2,684 subtests passed**.
- Combined runtime-plus-binding focused CPU result: **302 passed, 18 skipped, 2,726 subtests passed**.
- Master-off tests cover stock identity and bypass for sharded verification, prepared-next, ReplaySSM commit, GDN prefill graphs, resource reuse, and explicit child-switch overrides. Unsupported consumers preserve the full-vocabulary stock path.
- A no-simulation serving run completed GSM10 with **10/10** answers. An integrated serving run also completed a 53-request long-context replay.
- Layer-by-layer localization found no numerical difference before the ReplaySSM committed state. At that first difference, 233 of 5,898,240 BF16 elements differed, all within `atol=1e-6, rtol=2^-7`; this state is tolerance-equivalent, not bitwise-equivalent.
- In a real two-request TEP8 verify batch, all eight ranks compared 434,560 provider-slot logits and 57,344 hidden-state values with the stock computation and found zero bitwise differences.
- DEP8 with only the master switch enabled (runtime only, without Qwen3.5 plugin enablement) completed no-simulation greedy GSM10 with **10/10** answers.
- Greedy default verification, including requests carrying seeds, is bitwise identical to direct stock behavior.

@@ -221,3 +221,49 @@ def update_trtllm_mha_graph_metadata(
         BS_BLOCK=triton.next_power_of_2(bs),
         SKIP_PAGE_TABLE=1 if skip_page_table else 0,
     )
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _draft_step_seqlens_kernel(
+    seq_lens_ptr,  # [bs] int
+    cache_seqlens_ptr,  # [steps, cache_seqlens_stride] int32
+    cu_seqlens_k_ptr,  # [steps, cu_seqlens_k_stride] int32
+    bs,
+    first_offset,
+    cache_seqlens_stride,
+    cu_seqlens_k_stride,
+    BS_BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    # One program per draft step s: cache_seqlens = seq_lens + first_offset + s, and its
+    # cu_seqlens_k cumsum (cu_seqlens_k[s, 0] stays the preset 0).
+    s = tl.program_id(axis=0)
+    offs = tl.arange(0, BS_BLOCK)
+    mask = offs < bs
+    seqlens = tl.load(seq_lens_ptr + offs, mask=mask, other=0).to(tl.int32)
+    seqlens = tl.where(mask, seqlens + first_offset + s, 0)
+    tl.store(cache_seqlens_ptr + s * cache_seqlens_stride + offs, seqlens, mask=mask)
+    tl.store(
+        cu_seqlens_k_ptr + s * cu_seqlens_k_stride + 1 + offs,
+        tl.cumsum(seqlens, axis=0),
+        mask=mask,
+    )
+
+
+def update_draft_step_seqlens(
+    *, seq_lens, cache_seqlens, cu_seqlens_k, bs: int, steps: int, first_offset: int
+):
+    """The cache_seqlens / cu_seqlens_k rows of ``steps`` draft decode steps in one launch:
+    row s holds what ``update_trtllm_mha_graph_metadata`` writes at
+    ``seqlen_offset = first_offset + s``."""
+    if bs == 0 or steps == 0:
+        return
+    _draft_step_seqlens_kernel[(steps,)](
+        seq_lens,
+        cache_seqlens,
+        cu_seqlens_k,
+        bs,
+        first_offset,
+        cache_seqlens.stride(0),
+        cu_seqlens_k.stride(0),
+        BS_BLOCK=triton.next_power_of_2(bs),
+    )

+"""Length-sorted request groups for TRT-LLM decode attention, built once per forward.
+
+With ``SGLANG_TRTLLM_MHA_DECODE_SEQ_LEN_SPLITS`` above one, every decode attention call
+sorts the requests by KV length and gathers the query, block table and seq lens of each
+group before its FMHA launch. Only the query depends on the layer: the order and the
+gathered block tables and seq lens are the same for every call of a forward.
+``DecodeGroupPlans`` builds them at the first call and later calls reuse them, so a call
+keeps one query gather, the FMHA launches on contiguous slices, and one output scatter.
+The groups and their order are the stock ones, so the output is bitwise unchanged.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import Callable, NamedTuple, Optional
+
+import torch
+
+
+class DecodeGroupPlan(NamedTuple):
+    # [bs] request indices sorted by KV length (torch.argsort, as the stock path).
+    order: torch.Tensor
+    # [bs, max_pages] and [bs]: the block tables and seq lens in `order`.
+    block_tables: torch.Tensor
+    seq_lens: torch.Tensor
+
+
+class DecodeGroupPlans:
+    """Plans of the current forward, keyed by the metadata tensors a call passes in."""
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        self._plans: dict[tuple, DecodeGroupPlan] = {}
+
+    def reset(self) -> None:
+        # Call at every forward-metadata init: a plan is only valid within one forward,
+        # and buffers of the next forward may reuse the same addresses.
+        self._plans = {}
+
+    def get(
+        self, *, block_tables: torch.Tensor, seq_lens: torch.Tensor
+    ) -> DecodeGroupPlan:
+        key = (
+            block_tables.data_ptr(),
+            tuple(block_tables.shape),
+            seq_lens.data_ptr(),
+            seq_lens.shape[0],
+        )
+        plan = self._plans.get(key)
+        if plan is None:
+            order = torch.argsort(seq_lens)
+            plan = DecodeGroupPlan(
+                order=order,
+                block_tables=block_tables.index_select(0, order),
+                seq_lens=seq_lens.index_select(0, order),
+            )
+            self._plans[key] = plan
+        return plan
+
+
+def group_sizes(num_requests: int, num_splits: int) -> list[int]:
+    """Section sizes of torch.tensor_split(x, num_splits) for len(x) == num_requests."""
+    base, extra = divmod(num_requests, num_splits)
+    return [base + 1 if i < extra else base for i in range(num_splits)]
+
+
+def run_planned_groups(
+    *,
+    query: torch.Tensor,
+    plan: DecodeGroupPlan,
+    num_splits: int,
+    q_len_per_req: int,
+    out: Optional[torch.Tensor],
+    out_dtype: torch.dtype,
+    run_group: Callable[..., torch.Tensor],
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Run the length groups of `plan`; same groups and order as the per-call stock path.
+
+    ``run_group(query, block_tables, seq_lens, out)`` launches one FMHA and writes into
+    ``out``. Returns [num_tokens, num_heads, head_dim].
+    """
+    num_requests = plan.order.shape[0]
+    num_heads, head_dim = query.shape[-2], query.shape[-1]
+    query_by_request = query.view(num_requests, q_len_per_req, num_heads, head_dim)
+    sorted_query = query_by_request.index_select(0, plan.order)
+    sorted_output = torch.empty(
+        query_by_request.shape, dtype=out_dtype, device=query.device
+    )
+    start = 0
+    for size in group_sizes(num_requests, num_splits):
+        end = start + size
+        run_group(
+            sorted_query[start:end].reshape(-1, num_heads, head_dim),
+            plan.block_tables[start:end],
+            plan.seq_lens[start:end],
+            sorted_output[start:end].view(-1, num_heads, head_dim),
+        )
+        start = end
+    output_by_request = (
+        out.view_as(query_by_request)
+        if out is not None
+        else torch.empty_like(sorted_output)
+    )
+    output_by_request.index_copy_(0, plan.order, sorted_output)
+    return output_by_request.view(-1, num_heads, head_dim)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Greedy target sampling on vocabulary-sharded LM-head output.
+
+Each rank reduces its ``[rows, V / tp]`` shard to int64 keys. A small cross-rank
+exchange then picks the winning token, matching ``torch.argmax`` over gathered FP32
+logits bit for bit. Alternate numeric policies can produce compatible local keys and
+reuse :func:`reduce_sharded_token_keys` without owning the collective.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import logging
+from importlib import import_module
+from typing import Optional
+
+import msgspec
+import torch
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+
+from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+
+_provider_spec = import_module("sglang.kernels.plugin_kernels.nvidia.spec")
+_provider_vocab_shard = getattr(_provider_spec, "VocabShardView", None)
+if _provider_vocab_shard is None:
+
+    class VocabShard(msgspec.Struct, frozen=True):
+        """Columns [0, valid) are global token ids ``start + column``."""
+
+        start: int
+        valid: int
+        vocab_size: int
+
+else:
+    # When the optional binding contract is installed, expose its one canonical
+    # shard-view type.  Runtime-only builds retain the structurally identical
+    # local type above and never import a binding-only symbol eagerly.
+    VocabShard = _provider_vocab_shard
+
+
+def spec_allows_vocab_shards(spec) -> bool:
+    """Whether the server's verify rule can accept or reject on shard keys."""
+    return (
+        not spec.speculative_use_rejection_sampling
+        and spec.speculative_accept_threshold_single == 1.0
+        and spec.speculative_accept_threshold_acc == 1.0
+    )
+
+
+def sampling_allows_vocab_shards(
+    info, *, return_logprob: bool, has_local_keys: bool
+) -> bool:
+    """Whether a verify batch's sampling parameters can consume vocabulary shards.
+
+    Greedy rows are bitwise-preserving. Temperature-only rows need a local key
+    policy. Anything that reads or edits full logits needs the gathered logits.
+    """
+    return (
+        # A provider may decline after seeing its local shard.  Sanitizing that
+        # low-precision shard before the decline is not stock-equivalent: stock
+        # gathers to FP32 first, then sanitizes.  This diagnostic mode is rare,
+        # so keep its exact mutation order by entering the gathered path before
+        # invoking any optional local-key policy.
+        not (has_local_keys and envs.SGLANG_SANITIZE_NAN_LOGITS.get())
+        and not return_logprob
+        and info.acc_additive_penalties is None
+        and info.acc_scaling_penalties is None
+        and info.logit_bias is None
+        and (
+            info.is_all_greedy
+            or (
+                has_local_keys
+                and not (
+                    info.need_top_k_sampling
+                    or info.need_top_p_sampling
+                    or info.need_min_p_sampling
+                )
+            )
+        )
+    )
+
+
+# key of (-inf, token id 0xFFFFFFFF): below every real column's key
+_KEY_FLOOR = -2139095041 << 32
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _shard_key_kernel(
+    logits_ptr,
+    stride_row,
+    keys_ptr,
+    start,
+    valid,
+    vocab_size,
+    span,
+    KEY_FLOOR: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    # program (row, part): columns [part * span, (part + 1) * span) of the row's shard
+    row = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)
+    part = tl.program_id(1)
+    lo = part * span
+    hi = tl.minimum(lo + span, valid)
+    best = tl.full([BLOCK], KEY_FLOOR, tl.int64)
+    for off in range(lo, hi, BLOCK):
+        cols = off + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+        gid = start + cols
+        mask = (cols < hi) & (gid < vocab_size)
+        x = tl.load(
+            logits_ptr + row * stride_row + cols, mask=mask, other=float("-inf")
+        )
+        x = x.to(tl.float32)
+        # NaN never wins, as after sanitize_nan_logits; -0.0 ties +0.0 as in torch.argmax
+        x = tl.where(x == x, x, float("-inf")) + 0.0
+        bits = x.to(tl.int32, bitcast=True)
+        # monotone in x as a signed int32; the low word prefers the smaller token id
+        ordered = tl.where(bits < 0, bits ^ 0x7FFFFFFF, bits).to(tl.int64)
+        key = (ordered << 32) | (4294967295 - gid.to(tl.int64))
+        key = tl.where(mask, key, KEY_FLOOR)
+        best = tl.maximum(best, key)
+    tl.store(keys_ptr + row * tl.num_programs(1) + part, tl.max(best, axis=0))
+
+
+_KEY_BLOCK = 2048
+
+
+def key_splits(valid: int) -> int:
+    """Programs per row, padded even so a row spans whole multimem chunks."""
+    n = -(-valid // _KEY_BLOCK)
+    return n + (n & 1)
+
+
+def shard_keys(
+    logits: torch.Tensor,
+    shard: VocabShard,
+    splits: int = 1,
+    *,
+    temperatures: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    seeds: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """One int64 key per row of this rank's shard: (order-preserving FP32 bits of the
+    row's best value) << 32 | (0xFFFFFFFF - token id). ``splits > 1`` returns
+    ``[rows, splits]``, the best key from each column range. Greedy ignores existing
+    per-request seed material; numeric temperature policies use the local-key seam."""
+    if temperatures is not None:
+        raise ValueError("runtime shard_keys is greedy-only")
+    assert logits.stride(-1) == 1
+    rows = logits.shape[0]
+    keys = torch.empty(
+        (rows, splits) if splits > 1 else (rows,),
+        dtype=torch.int64,
+        device=logits.device,
+    )
+    if rows == 0:
+        return keys
+    _shard_key_kernel[(rows, splits)](
+        logits,
+        logits.stride(0),
+        keys,
+        shard.start,
+        shard.valid,
+        shard.vocab_size,
+        -(-shard.valid // splits),
+        KEY_FLOOR=_KEY_FLOOR,
+        BLOCK=_KEY_BLOCK,
+        num_warps=8,
+    )
+    return keys
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _keys_to_tokens_kernel(
+    keys_ptr,
+    tokens_ptr,
+    stride_rank,
+    stride_row,
+    world,
+    parts,
+    KEY_FLOOR: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_R: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_P: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    row = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)
+    r = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_R)[:, None]
+    p = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_P)[None, :]
+    k = tl.load(
+        keys_ptr + row * stride_row + r * stride_rank + p,
+        mask=(r < world) & (p < parts),
+        other=KEY_FLOOR,
+    )
+    best = tl.max(tl.max(k, axis=1), axis=0)
+    tl.store(tokens_ptr + row, 4294967295 - (best & 4294967295))
+
+
+def _reduce_keys(keys, rows, world, parts, stride_rank, stride_row) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """[rows] token ids from the keys at keys[row * stride_row + rank * stride_rank + part]
+    (int64 elements), the max over every rank and part of a row, in one launch."""
+    tokens = torch.empty(rows, dtype=torch.int64, device=keys.device)
+    if rows:
+        _keys_to_tokens_kernel[(rows,)](
+            keys,
+            tokens,
+            stride_rank,
+            stride_row,
+            world,
+            parts,
+            KEY_FLOOR=_KEY_FLOOR,
+            BLOCK_R=triton.next_power_of_2(world),
+            BLOCK_P=triton.next_power_of_2(parts),
+            num_warps=1,
+        )
+    return tokens
+
+
+def keys_to_tokens(
+    gathered: torch.Tensor, tp_size: int, splits: int = 1
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """[tp * rows * splits] keys of all ranks (rank-major) -> [rows] int64 token ids."""
+    if splits == 1:
+        best = gathered.view(tp_size, -1).amax(dim=0)
+        return 0xFFFFFFFF - (best & 0xFFFFFFFF)
+    rows = gathered.numel() // (tp_size * splits)
+    return _reduce_keys(gathered, rows, tp_size, splits, rows * splits, splits)
+
+
+# The key exchange's multimem state is built by the first eager, rank-lockstep call.
+# A row of one rank is ``width`` int64 values (four BF16 values each).
+_MC_MAX_ROWS = 1024
+_mc_state = None
+_mc_width = 0
+
+
+def _tp_group_in_one_nvlink_domain(tp_group, device) -> bool:
+    """Whether every TP rank shares one NVLink address space.
+
+    A GB200/GB300 NVL72 fabric spans multiple hosts, so host co-location is not
+    the capability boundary.  Reuse the custom-all-reduce topology probe: it
+    checks full NVLink connectivity on one host and the NVML fabric clique for
+    a multi-host group.  The builders below still require symmetric-memory
+    rendezvous and a nonzero multicast pointer before engaging the fast path.
+    """
+    if tp_group.world_size <= 1:
+        return False
+    from sglang.srt.distributed.device_communicators.custom_all_reduce_utils import (
+        in_one_nvlink_domain,
+    )
+
+    return in_one_nvlink_domain(tp_group.cpu_group, torch.device(device))
+
+
+def _mc_build(tp_group, hidden_size: int, device):
+    """The multimem state, or False (NCCL keeps the exchange) when the buffer has no
+    multicast mapping, e.g. a TP group spanning distinct NVLink fabric domains."""
+    if not _tp_group_in_one_nvlink_domain(tp_group, device):
+        logger.warning(
+            "Sharded verify multimem disabled because the TP group is outside "
+            "one NVLink fabric domain; using NCCL"
+        )
+        return False
+    from sglang.srt.distributed.device_communicators import triton_symm_mem_ag
+
+    try:
+        state = triton_symm_mem_ag.create_state(
+            tp_group.device_group,
+            tp_group.rank_in_group,
+            max_tokens=_MC_MAX_ROWS,
+            hidden_size=hidden_size,
+            device=device,
+        )
+    except Exception as e:  # rendezvous refused: every rank sees the same failure
+        logger.warning("Sharded verify multimem setup failed; using NCCL: %s", e)
+        return False
+    if state.symm_mem_hdl.multicast_ptr == 0:
+        logger.warning("Sharded verify has no multicast mapping; using NCCL")
+        return False
+    logger.info(
+        "Sharded verify MC multimem exchange enabled (world_size=%d)",
+        tp_group.world_size,
+    )
+    return state
+
+
+def _mc_gather_keys(keys: torch.Tensor, tp_group) -> Optional[torch.Tensor]:
+    """[rows] or [rows, parts] int64 keys of every rank -> [rows] token ids, by one
+    multimem all-gather (rows of at least 2 int64: a single key goes twice); None when
+    there is no multicast state."""
+    global _mc_state, _mc_width
+    from sglang.srt.distributed.device_communicators import triton_symm_mem_ag
+
+    world, rows = tp_group.world_size, keys.shape[0]
+    if keys.dim() == 1:
+        keys = torch.stack((keys, keys), dim=1)
+    width = keys.shape[1]
+    if _mc_state is None:
+        _mc_state = _mc_build(tp_group, 4 * width * world, keys.device)
+        _mc_width = width
+    if _mc_state is False:
+        return None
+    assert width == _mc_width, (width, _mc_width)
+    out = triton_symm_mem_ag.all_gather_inner(
+        _mc_state, keys.view(torch.bfloat16), 4 * width * world, safe=False
+    )
+    # rows of the symmetric buffer; rank r's keys at int64 column width * r
+    out = out.view(torch.int64)
+    return _reduce_keys(out, rows, world, width, width, out.stride(0))
+
+
+# Epoch-tagged exchange of one key per row. The low/high halves use two 64-bit
+# words whose high halves carry a nonzero 32-bit tag.  A separate cursor rotates
+# the three slots, so wrapping the wire tag never reuses the preceding slot.
+_LL_SLOTS = 3
+_LL_MAX_ROWS = 64
+# Ranks are aligned before the poll (a collective, eager or captured), so a long wait
+# means a peer that is slow or gone. It is bounded by wall time on the scale of a
+# process-group timeout (torch's default) rather than by a spin count, and reported.
+_LL_TIMEOUT_NS = 600 * 10**9
+_LL_WARN_NS = 5 * 10**9
+_LL_TRAP_GRACE_NS = 10**9
+_LL_TIME_CHECK_SPINS = 1024
+# Host-mapped records the poll writes for the watcher: [warning, timeout] of
+# [state, rank, tag, slot, rows, parts, missing-rank bitmask, waited ns].
+_LL_RECORD = 8
+_ll_state = None
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _ll_st_b64(addr, val, mask):
+    return tl.inline_asm_elementwise(
+        """
+        {
+            .reg .pred %p0;
+            setp.eq.s32 %p0, $3, 1;
+            @!%p0 bra end;
+            multimem.st.relaxed.sys.global.b64 [$1], $2;
+            end:
+        }
+        """,
+        "=r,l,l,r",
+        args=[addr, val, mask.to(tl.int32)],
+        dtype=tl.uint32,
+        is_pure=False,
+        pack=1,
+    )
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _ll_ld_b64(addr, mask):
+    return tl.inline_asm_elementwise(
+        """
+        {
+            .reg .pred %p0;
+            setp.eq.s32 %p0, $2, 1;
+            mov.u64 $0, 0;
+            @!%p0 bra end;
+            ld.relaxed.sys.global.u64 $0, [$1];
+            end:
+        }
+        """,
+        "=l,l,r",
+        args=[addr, mask.to(tl.int32)],
+        dtype=tl.uint64,
+        is_pure=False,
+        pack=1,
+    )
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _ll_trap():
+    tl.inline_asm_elementwise("trap;", "=r", [], dtype=tl.int32, is_pure=False, pack=1)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _ll_now():
+    return tl.inline_asm_elementwise(
+        "mov.u64 $0, %globaltimer;", "=l", [], dtype=tl.int64, is_pure=False, pack=1
+    )
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _ll_fence():
+    tl.inline_asm_elementwise(
+        "fence.sc.sys;", "=r", [], dtype=tl.int32, is_pure=False, pack=1
+    )
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _ll_record(diag_addr, base, state, rank, tag, slot, rows, parts, missing, waited):
+    # fields first, then the state word the watcher polls
+    d = diag_addr.to(tl.pointer_type(tl.int64)) + base
+    i = tl.arange(0, 8)
+    v = tl.zeros([8], tl.int64)
+    v = tl.where(i == 1, rank, v)
+    v = tl.where(i == 2, tag.to(tl.int64), v)
+    v = tl.where(i == 3, slot, v)
+    v = tl.where(i == 4, rows, v)
+    v = tl.where(i == 5, parts, v)
+    v = tl.where(i == 6, missing, v)
+    v = tl.where(i == 7, waited, v)
+    tl.store(d + i, v, mask=i > 0)
+    _ll_fence()
+    tl.store(d + i, tl.full([8], state, tl.int64), mask=i == 0)
+    _ll_fence()
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _ll_keys_kernel(
+    keys_ptr,
+    parts,
+    rows,
+    mc_addr,
+    uc_addr,
+    epoch_ptr,
+    tokens_ptr,
+    diag_addr,
+    warn_ns,
+    timeout_ns,
+    RANK: tl.constexpr,
+    WORLD: tl.constexpr,
+    MAXR: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_R: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_P: tl.constexpr,
+    KEY_FLOOR: tl.constexpr,
+    TIME_CHECK_SPINS: tl.constexpr,
+    TRAP_GRACE_NS: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    # The wire format has exactly 32 tag bits.  Reinterpret the signed storage
+    # before widening, skip zero (the buffer's initial value), and keep slot
+    # rotation independent from tag wrap.  Both counters stay device-owned so
+    # CUDA graph replay never introduces a host synchronization.
+    last_tag = tl.load(epoch_ptr).to(tl.uint32, bitcast=True).to(tl.uint64)
+    tag = last_tag + 1
+    tag = tl.where(tag == 4294967296, 1, tag)
+    slot = ((tl.load(epoch_ptr + 1) + 1) % 3).to(tl.int64)
+    r = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_R)
+    p = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_P)
+    rmask = r < rows
+    k = tl.load(
+        keys_ptr + r[:, None] * parts + p[None, :],
+        mask=rmask[:, None] & (p[None, :] < parts),
+        other=KEY_FLOOR,
+    )
+    key = tl.max(k, axis=1).to(tl.uint64, bitcast=True)
+    tagw = tag << 32
+    mc = mc_addr.to(tl.pointer_type(tl.uint64))
+    word = ((slot * WORLD + RANK) * MAXR + r) * 2
+    _ll_st_b64(mc + word, (key & 0xFFFFFFFF) | tagw, rmask)
+    _ll_st_b64(mc + word + 1, (key >> 32) | tagw, rmask)
+    s = tl.arange(0, WORLD)
+    m2 = rmask[None, :] & (s[:, None] < WORLD)
+    uc = uc_addr.to(tl.pointer_type(tl.uint64))
+    words = ((slot * WORLD + s[:, None]) * MAXR + r[None, :]) * 2
+    # a CTA barrier before each block-wide count of the poll: without them some warps left it
+    # on a stale count and took words a slot held from an earlier launch
+    tl.debug_barrier()
+    lo = _ll_ld_b64(uc + words, m2)
+    hi = _ll_ld_b64(uc + words + 1, m2)
+    ok = (((lo >> 32) == tag) & ((hi >> 32) == tag)) | (~m2)
+    pending = tl.sum(1 - ok.to(tl.int32))
+    spins = 0
+    warned = 0
+    start = _ll_now()
+    while pending > 0:
+        tl.debug_barrier()
+        lo = _ll_ld_b64(uc + words, m2)
+        hi = _ll_ld_b64(uc + words + 1, m2)
+        ok = (((lo >> 32) == tag) & ((hi >> 32) == tag)) | (~m2)
+        pending = tl.sum(1 - ok.to(tl.int32))
+        spins += 1
+        if (pending > 0) & (spins % TIME_CHECK_SPINS == 0):
+            # one thread's clock, so every warp takes the same branch
+            waited = tl.max(tl.where(r == 0, _ll_now() - start, 0), axis=0)
+            late = tl.sum(1 - ok.to(tl.int32), axis=1)
+            missing = tl.sum(tl.where(late > 0, 1 << s, 0).to(tl.int64), axis=0)
+            if (warned == 0) & (waited > warn_ns):
+                _ll_record(
+                    diag_addr, 0, 1, RANK, tag, slot, rows, parts, missing, waited
+                )
+                warned = 1
+            if waited > timeout_ns:
+                _ll_record(
+                    diag_addr,
+                    8,
+                    2,
+                    RANK,
+                    tag,
+                    slot,
+                    rows,
+                    parts,
+                    missing,
+                    waited,
+                )
+                # let the host watcher log the record before the context dies
+                held = _ll_now()
+                while _ll_now() - held < TRAP_GRACE_NS:
+                    spins += 1
+                _ll_trap()
+    got = (((hi & 0xFFFFFFFF) << 32) | (lo & 0xFFFFFFFF)).to(tl.int64, bitcast=True)
+    best = tl.max(tl.where(m2, got, KEY_FLOOR), axis=0)
+    tl.store(tokens_ptr + r, 4294967295 - (best & 4294967295), mask=rmask)
+    tl.store(epoch_ptr, tag.to(tl.uint32).to(tl.int32, bitcast=True))
+    tl.store(epoch_ptr + 1, slot.to(tl.int32))
+
+
+def _ll_build(tp_group, device):
+    """The LL exchange's symmetric buffer (zeroed before any peer can write it) and epoch, or
+    False (the other exchanges keep the call) when it has no multicast mapping."""
+    if not _tp_group_in_one_nvlink_domain(tp_group, device):
+        logger.warning(
+            "Sharded verify LL disabled because the TP group is outside one "
+            "NVLink fabric domain; using NCCL"
+        )
+        return False
+    import torch.distributed as dist
+    import torch.distributed._symmetric_memory as symm_mem
+
+    world = tp_group.world_size
+    try:
+        with torch.inference_mode(False), torch.no_grad():
+            buf = symm_mem.empty(
+                (_LL_SLOTS * world * _LL_MAX_ROWS * 2,),
+                dtype=torch.int64,
+                device=device,
+            )
+        hdl = symm_mem.rendezvous(buf, group=tp_group.device_group)
+    except Exception as e:
+        logger.warning("Sharded verify LL setup failed; trying other exchanges: %s", e)
+        return False
+    if hdl.multicast_ptr == 0:
+        logger.warning("Sharded verify LL exchange has no multicast mapping")
+        return False
+    buf.zero_()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize(device)
+    dist.barrier(group=tp_group.cpu_group)
+    # [last nonzero wire tag bits, independent slot cursor]
+    epoch = torch.zeros(2, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    diag = _ll_watch(world)
+    # stays zero: summed only to align the ranks before an eager poll
+    align = torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
+    logger.info(
+        "Sharded verify LL multimem exchange enabled (world_size=%d)",
+        tp_group.world_size,
+    )
+    return (buf, hdl, epoch, diag, align)
+
+
+def _ll_describe(record, world: int) -> str:
+    _, rank, tag, slot, rows, parts, missing, waited = record
+    peers = [peer for peer in range(world) if missing >> peer & 1]
+    return (
+        f"TP rank {rank} waited {waited / 1e9:.1f} s for ranks {peers} "
+        f"(tag={tag}, slot={slot}, rows={rows}, parts={parts})"
+    )
+
+
+def _ll_watch(world: int, poll_s: float = 0.1) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Pinned records the LL poll writes, and a daemon thread that logs them.
+
+    The host reads them without touching the GPU stream, so neither the eager
+    path nor a captured graph gains a synchronization, and a timeout record is
+    still readable after the poll traps the context."""
+    import threading
+    import time
+
+    diag = torch.zeros(2 * _LL_RECORD, dtype=torch.int64, pin_memory=True)
+
+    def watch():
+        warned = None
+        while True:
+            time.sleep(poll_s)
+            warning, timeout = diag[:_LL_RECORD].tolist(), diag[_LL_RECORD:].tolist()
+            if timeout[0]:
+                logger.error(
+                    "Sharded verify LL exchange timed out: %s. Those ranks never "
+                    "reached this exchange; the poll traps the CUDA context.",
+                    _ll_describe(timeout, world),
+                )
+                return
+            if warning[0] and warning[2] != warned:
+                warned = warning[2]
+                logger.warning(
+                    "Sharded verify LL exchange is waiting: %s",
+                    _ll_describe(warning, world),
+                )
+
+    threading.Thread(target=watch, name="sharded-verify-ll-watch", daemon=True).start()
+    return diag
+
+
+def _ll_keys(keys: torch.Tensor, tp_group) -> Optional[torch.Tensor]:
+    """[rows] or [rows, parts] int64 keys of every rank -> [rows] token ids in one launch, or None
+    when the LL exchange is unavailable."""
+    global _ll_state
+    if _ll_state is None:
+        _ll_state = _ll_build(tp_group, keys.device)
+    if _ll_state is False:
+        return None
+    buf, hdl, epoch, diag, align = _ll_state
+    if not torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing():
+        # Out of a graph nothing lines the ranks up before the poll, and one still
+        # on the host (a first-use build, a slow step) would run its clock out. A
+        # collective parks the early ranks' streams instead, with no deadline; a
+        # captured round's earlier all-reduce already does this.
+        tp_group.all_reduce(align)
+    rows = keys.shape[0]
+    parts = keys.shape[1] if keys.dim() == 2 else 1
+    tokens = torch.empty(rows, dtype=torch.int64, device=keys.device)
+    _ll_keys_kernel[(1,)](
+        keys,
+        parts,
+        rows,
+        hdl.multicast_ptr,
+        hdl.buffer_ptrs[hdl.rank],
+        epoch,
+        tokens,
+        diag.data_ptr(),
+        _LL_WARN_NS,
+        _LL_TIMEOUT_NS,
+        RANK=hdl.rank,
+        WORLD=tp_group.world_size,
+        MAXR=_LL_MAX_ROWS,
+        BLOCK_R=max(16, triton.next_power_of_2(rows)),
+        BLOCK_P=max(2, triton.next_power_of_2(parts)),
+        KEY_FLOOR=_KEY_FLOOR,
+        TIME_CHECK_SPINS=_LL_TIME_CHECK_SPINS,
+        TRAP_GRACE_NS=_LL_TRAP_GRACE_NS,
+        num_warps=4,
+    )
+    return tokens
+
+
+def sharded_target_tokens(
+    logits: torch.Tensor,
+    shard: VocabShard,
+    tp_group,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """[rows] token ids over the whole vocabulary from every rank's logits shard."""
+    # The final TP rank may have fewer valid vocabulary columns than its padded
+    # local LM-head output.  Every rank must nevertheless enter the collective
+    # with the same key shape, so derive the split count from the rank-uniform
+    # padded local width; ``shard.valid`` still masks the kernel's tail.
+    splits = key_splits(logits.shape[-1])
+    keys = shard_keys(logits, shard, splits)
+    return reduce_sharded_token_keys(keys, tp_group, splits=splits)
+
+
+def reduce_sharded_token_keys(
+    keys: torch.Tensor,
+    tp_group,
+    *,
+    splits: int,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Reduce provider-neutral local token keys to one global token per row.
+
+    ``keys`` is contiguous int64 with shape ``[rows, splits]`` (or ``[rows]``
+    for one split). Larger keys win. Their high 32 bits encode a monotone score;
+    their low 32 bits are ``0xffffffff - global_token_id``, so ties pick the
+    smaller token exactly as ``torch.argmax`` does. Runtime owns the
+    LL/multimem/NCCL exchange while callers own the numeric policy that produced
+    each local key.
+    """
+    if splits <= 0:
+        raise ValueError(f"splits must be positive, got {splits}")
+    if keys.dtype != torch.int64:
+        raise TypeError(f"keys must have dtype torch.int64, got {keys.dtype}")
+    if not keys.is_contiguous():
+        raise ValueError("keys must be contiguous")
+    if splits == 1 and keys.ndim != 1:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"one split: keys shape {tuple(keys.shape)} is incompatible with splits=1"
+        )
+    if splits > 1 and (keys.ndim != 2 or keys.shape[1] != splits):
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"keys shape {tuple(keys.shape)} is incompatible with splits={splits}"
+        )
+    world = tp_group.world_size
+    power_of_two_world = world > 0 and (world & (world - 1)) == 0

+        speculative_accept_threshold_acc=1.0,
+    )
+
+
+class _FakeGroup:
+    """all_gather_into_tensor over shards held on one device, rank order."""
+
+    def __init__(self, shards):
+        self.shards, self.world_size = shards, len(shards)
+
+    def all_gather_into_tensor(self, output, input):
+        output.copy_(torch.cat([s.reshape(-1) for s in self.shards]))
+
+
+class TestShardedPolicy(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_temperature_decline_gathers_then_enters_stock_without_early_rng(self):
+        sampling = _sampling_info(greedy=False)
+        shard = VocabShard(start=0, valid=5, vocab_size=5)
+        logits = SimpleNamespace(
+            next_token_logits=_verify_logits().clone(),
+            next_token_logits_vocab_shard=shard,
+        )
+        batch = _verify_batch(sampling)
+        group = SimpleNamespace(world_size=1)
+        group.all_gather_into_tensor = lambda output, value: output.copy_(value)
+        parallel = SimpleNamespace(tp_group=group, attn_tp_group=group)
+        events = []
+        state_before = torch.random.get_rng_state().clone()
+
+        def local_keys(_view):
+            events.append("local")
+            self.assertTrue(torch.equal(torch.random.get_rng_state(), state_before))
+            return None
+
+        original_gather = eagle_utils.gather_full_logits
+
+        def gather(*args, **kwargs):
+            events.append("gather")
+            return original_gather(*args, **kwargs)
+
+        def stock_sample(**kwargs):
+            events.append("stock")
+            self.assertFalse(torch.equal(torch.random.get_rng_state(), state_before))
+            kwargs["predicts"].zero_()
+            kwargs["accept_index"].fill_(-1)
+            kwargs["accept_token_num"].zero_()
+
+        with (
+            patch.object(eagle_utils, "_is_cuda", True),
+            patch.object(eagle_utils, "_is_cpu", False),
+            patch.object(eagle_utils, "_is_hip", False),
+            patch.object(eagle_utils, "_is_xpu", False),
+            patch.object(eagle_utils, "get_spec", return_value=_runtime_spec()),
+            patch.object(eagle_utils, "gather_full_logits", side_effect=gather),
+            patch.object(
+                eagle_utils,
+                "tree_speculative_sampling_target_only",
+                side_effect=stock_sample,
+            ),
+            patch("sglang.srt.runtime_context.get_parallel", return_value=parallel),
+            patch(
+                "sglang.srt.layers.dp_attention.is_dp_attention_enabled",
+                return_value=False,
+            ),
+        ):
+            eagle_utils.eagle_sample(
+                _verify_tree(),
+                batch,
+                logits,
+                local_keys=local_keys,
+            )
+
+        self.assertEqual(events, ["local", "gather", "stock"])
+        self.assertIsNone(logits.next_token_logits_vocab_shard)
+        self.assertEqual(tuple(logits.next_token_logits.shape), (6, 5))
+
+
+def _sharded_tokens(full, tp, split=False):
+    width = -(-full.shape[1] // tp)
+    splits = key_splits(width) if split else 1
+    keys = []
+    for rank in range(tp):
+        start = rank * width
+        part = full[:, start : start + width].contiguous()
+        shard = VocabShard(start=start, valid=part.shape[1], vocab_size=full.shape[1])
+        keys.append(shard_keys(part, shard, splits).view(-1))
+    return keys_to_tokens(torch.cat(keys), tp, splits)
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(torch.cuda.is_available(), "needs CUDA")
+class TestShardedGreedy(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_matches_argmax(self):
+        generator = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(0)
+        full = (
+            torch.randn(7, VOCAB, device="cuda", generator=generator) * 4
+        ).bfloat16()
+        peak = full.float().max() + 1
+        full[0, 5] = full[0, VOCAB - 3] = peak
+        full[1].fill_(1.5)
+        full[2].zero_()
+        want = torch.argmax(full.float(), dim=-1)
+        for split in (False, True):
+            self.assertTrue(torch.equal(_sharded_tokens(full, 8, split=split), want))
+
+    def test_exchange_falls_back_to_collective(self):
+        full = torch.randn(7, 4096, device="cuda").bfloat16()
+        shards = list(full.split(2048, dim=1))
+        parts = key_splits(shards[0].shape[1])
+        keys = [
+            shard_keys(
+                part,
+                VocabShard(rank * 2048, part.shape[1], full.shape[1]),
+                splits=parts,
+            )
+            for rank, part in enumerate(shards)
+        ]
+        with (
+            patch.object(sharded_verify, "_ll_keys", return_value=None) as ll,
+            patch.object(sharded_verify, "_mc_gather_keys", return_value=None) as mc,
+        ):
+            got = sharded_target_tokens(
+                shards[0],
+                VocabShard(0, shards[0].shape[1], full.shape[1]),
+                _FakeGroup(keys),
+            )
+        ll.assert_called_once()
+        mc.assert_called_once()
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(got, torch.argmax(full.float(), dim=-1)))
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(torch.cuda.is_available(), "needs CUDA")
+class TestGatherFullLogits(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_matches_concat_slice_cast(self):
+        # the fallback must rebuild the stock gathered logits exactly: rank-major
+        # vocabulary columns, cut to the vocabulary, FP32
+        full = torch.randn(7, 1000, device="cuda").bfloat16()
+        for tp in (2, 8):
+            with self.subTest(tp=tp):
+                width = -(-1000 // tp)
+                padded = torch.nn.functional.pad(full, (0, width * tp - 1000))
+                shards = list(padded.split(width, dim=1))
+                shard = VocabShard(start=0, valid=width, vocab_size=1000)
+                got = gather_full_logits(shards[0], shard, _FakeGroup(shards))
+                self.assertTrue(torch.equal(got, full.float()))
+
+
+_TEMPERATURE_ONLY = dict(is_all_greedy=False)
+_AGENTX_SAMPLING = dict(
+    is_all_greedy=False, need_top_k_sampling=True, need_top_p_sampling=True
+)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
